name: Comites seniores (palatina)

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: Raise Banner
abilities.text: Increases your general's area of influence and improves the army's defence for an extended period.

abilities.name: Steady
abilities.text: Improves the unit's ability to defend at the cost of their mobility.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: The name «Comites» can be translated from Latin as «companions»; more literally - battle companions/comrades-in-arms of the Emperor. All units of Comites in the Notitia Dignitatum are cavalry; moreover, of the eleven, all but two are palatine units. Ammianus Marcellinus gives (18.9.3) a unit of Comites, without further distinction, as being amongst the defenders at the siege of Amida in 359AD; likewise mounted Comites are mentioned without further distinction at 15.4.19. Inscriptional evidence for what has been taken to be the Comites comes from the cemetery at Colonia Iulia Concordia (modern Portogruaro in Veneto, Italy), which produced an inscription, mentioning an officer of the EQUITUM COMITIS SENI SAGIT, which expands to the «equitum Comit[um] seni(orum) sagit(tariorum)».
history: Rome’s Empire became so large that in its later period the Emperor could not be everywhere at once. As such he appointed ‘Comites’, trusted, high-ranking military and administrative figures who ran certain parts of the Empire in his stead. ‘Comes’ – the singular - is Latin for ‘Companion’, used here in direct reference to the Companions of Alexander the Great, the most trusted lieutenants of the greatest military leader the world had yet seen (and someone all Roman Emperors aspired to be like). The Comites were the Emperor’s own inner circle, the leading officials of the Empire, wielding posts of myriad descriptions and reasonability, from the ‘Comes Britanniarum’, who was in charge of Roman Britain’s defence, to the ‘Comes Sacrae Vestis’ – master of the Emperor’s wardrobe!
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
